data.name: Henrik
data.gender_notes: Henrik is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Norse name Heimirikr, meaning 'ruler of the home' or 'ruler of the people'. In Christian tradition, Henrik can also be a variation of Henry, which has Hebrew roots and means 'house of Henry' or 'home of the ruler'. The name Henrik carries the meaning “Ruler of the home” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Henrik usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the home and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of leadership and protection within the family and community.
data.etymology: Henrik belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the home.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Henrik total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: הנריק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הנריק הוא שם שמקורו בשם העברי 'חנריק' או 'הנריק', שהוא צורה משובשת של השם 'חבריק' או 'כנריק', שפירושו 'המלך השולט בביתו כמשיח'. השם קשור לאמונה היהודית והנוצרית כאחד, ומשמעותו עמוקה ורעיונית.

in_greek.name: Χένρικ
in_greek.long_meaning: Χένρικ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος 'Heinrich', που προέρχεται από το γερμανικό 'Heinrich', από το παλαιότερο 'Hainrich', που σημαίνει 'Ο βασιλιάς του οίκου του'. Το όνομα έχει σχέση με την χριστιανική παράδοση και χρησιμοποιήθηκε από πολλούς βασιλιάδες και ευγενείς στην Ευρώπη.

in_latin.name: Henricus
in_latin.long_meaning: Henricus est forma latina nominis 'Heinrich', quod significat 'Rex domus suae'. Nomen habet originem in traditione christiana et germanica, et fuit nomen multorum regum et principum in Europa.

in_english.name: Henrik
in_english.meaning: Estate ruler or lord of the manor
in_english.long_meaning: Henrik is a Christian name derived from the Germanic 'Heinrich', meaning 'estate ruler' or 'lord of the manor'. It originates from the Old High German 'hein' (home) and 'rich' (ruler), and has been used by many European monarchs and nobles throughout history. The name carries connotations of leadership, power, and responsibility, reflecting its origins in Christian and feudal traditions.

data.cultural_impact: Henrik holds significant historical and cultural importance in various European nations, most notably Scandinavia and Germany. It is a common name found across generations and is celebrated for its connection to the Tudors, Habsburgs, and other influential European families.
data.spiritual_significance: Henrik, in its spiritual context, symbolizes the divine stewardship of a household or community. It invokes the ideas of leadership, protection, and nurturing to ensure the well-being of those under one's care. In Christianity, Henrik can be seen as a reminder of God's care as a loving ruler and protector in our daily lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Henrik derives from the Germanic name Heimirik, meaning "ruler of the home" or "rule of the house." This name reflects the importance of family and domestic life in Christian values.

historical_references.reference: Henrik I, also known as Henrik Fiskeskar, was a Danish king who ruled from 1157 to 1182. He was the second son of King Valdemar the Great and contributed significantly to the development of the Danish monarchy. Henrik I extended Danish rule over the northern part of Jutland and secured the southern border against the Wends. He also established the first Danish bishoprics in the country, including the Archbishopric of Lund, which would later become the center of the Danish church.

Henrik VIII, also known as Henry Tudor, was the King of England from 1509 to 1547. He is best known for his six marriages and for his role in the separation of the Church of England from the Roman Catholic Church. This separation led to the establishment of the Anglican Church and the English Reformation. Henrik VIII's reign marked a significant turning point in English history and paved the way for the modern British state.
